crossing-wet.prompt: Produce one original, full-bleed 16:9 1860s maritime plein-air oil and gouache painting on fine linen for a historical point-and-click adventure. Think a real painter at a windswept place, with confident expressive flat bristle marks, great planes of colour, fine selective detail about things human hands have worn or made; strong non-photographic pictorial design and distinct local atmosphere, intelligible on a telephone. NOT a tracing or recolouring: invent new shapes, material grain, cloud formations, brushstrokes and lighting. Use the supplied reference ONLY as an immovable stage blueprint. Match its straight broadside framing and foreground walk plane, no shift, crop, tilt or lens change. Fixed world geometry! Cast, inventory and dialogue will be composited later: no people, no readable lettering, labels, watermarks, border, UI, loose pickups, modern fittings, or new foreground obstacles. Coordinates below in percent (x,y) of whole painting, origin upper left; do not print numbers. A night watch in Foveaux's southern waters, seen from inside a small open wooden ship's boat. A rolling diagonal of viridian sea a few inches beyond the gunwale, behind it distant silvery violet rain withdrawing and threads of luminous moonlight on crests. Sky indigo with a break of pewter blue and warmer bone canvas standing out against it; no orange sunset or land dominating. Look atmospheric and astonishing, but wood, ropes and sail legible at phone size. Preserve this source exact side-on theatre geometry, rail around y60–62 and solid closed bulwark from there down to y74, unbroken walkable sole x6–93 from y75–90. The centered mast is at x44, rope belayed at x26,y55, tiller sticks out left x4–20,y54–59; second halyard near (44.1,55.9). Keep a HUGE natural-flax sail occupying upper right, EXACT angled foot sewn to a long boom from (47,33) to (99,12), with exactly ONE small jagged dark wind tear INSIDE its canvas at x76 y13.9, about 4% of picture width. It must be a VISIBLE rip directly above the foot of the sail. In the cockpit sole at x66.4 y75.3 paint a small, distinct pool of sloshed green/pewter water straddling the floorboard seam, 11% wide, 3% tall. No other standing deck water, all floorboards around it clearly visible. Entire horizon at y45, narrow band of ocean. Keep original mast, tiller, ropes, rail and plane underfoot rigidly registered to the blueprint.
